result.title: LocateAnyMesh: Grounding 3D Mesh Queries in 2D Images with Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Textured 3D meshes specify object geometry and appearance, making them a natural query for finding a particular asset in an image. We introduce LocateAnyMesh, a vision-language model that uses the mesh itself as part of its prompt. A frozen 3D encoder maps colored surface points to a compact token sequence, which a learned connector places alongside image and instruction tokens. We evaluate two grounding models with PPAT mesh tokens: LAM-Select selects image-region proposals, while LAM-Direct predicts coordinates directly. Neither requires rendered query views or view-template matching. New objects require a single encoder pass and no object-specific fine-tuning. LAM-Select improves localization on the reported real-image suites and the official BOP YCB-V evaluation. Secondary experiments compare mesh encoders, and a LAM-Direct study isolates surface color. A single-seed LAM-Select continuation supplies pointing and mesh-only description evidence without replacing the reported localization model. The results support mesh tokens as a query representation, with remaining limitations in presence decisions, identity binding, proposal coverage, and descriptive fidelity.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 LocateAnyMesh，用冻结的 3D 编码器把纹理网格的表面点编码为 token 序列，经 connector 与图像、指令 token 拼接，让 VLM 在图像中定位对应物体，并比较「选区域提案」与「直接回归坐标」两种定位头。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是以网格为查询的 3D 资产定位/匹配任务，核心在于跨模态 token 对齐与检索式定位，不涉及 latent 推理状态、证据获取、动态计算或停止决策；标准模态适配器设计也未提供针对 LVR 的具体可核查线索，故排除。
